final.result:
**Probably not, or at least we can't tell yet.** The earlier evaluation doesn't cover data like ours.

- **What we tested before:** a memory note from the telemetry project (2026-03-20, from the project wiki) records that the Ostrich 0.9 benchmark got 4.1x compression. That was only on text log files under 1 MB, using one core.
- **Our archives:** protobuf-encoded binary frames, 40–300 MB per file. Binary data and files over 1 MB were both left out of that benchmark.

So the 4.1x figure doesn't carry over. Binary protobuf usually compresses much less than text logs. Before deciding, I'd run Ostrich on a few real nightly archives and compare its compression ratio and speed, on more than one core, against zstd or xz.
